verdict: In 12 mocked drops (13 files, 1.4 GiB, 186 parts each) the ten longest frames of both traces hold no upload-path work over 14 ms, and every frame over 100 ms that was attributed had no script and 0 ms blocking: the page main thread was idle while the frame waited outside the page. No Studio code was changed.
whyS38DoesNotPointAtTheDrop: S3.8 recorded one capture of 5,401 s (312,414 frames) while all 17 uploads were retained by 294 s; its longest task was 111 ms against a 1,084 ms worst frame, so its slow frames are neither placed in the drop nor main-thread work.

comparison.hypothesis: CPU contention alone makes the drop slow frames
comparison.change: 28 busy threads, one per logical core, for the whole drop
comparison.result: rejected: 33 captures, 0 over 100 ms, max 61 ms; the drop took 420 s instead of 157 s

before.note: plain: its one 567 ms frame came while an 8 GB trace analysis ran on the same machine

after.note: no code change; the same drop measured again, nothing else of this task running

totals.capturesWithAFrameOver250ms: 6 captures in 4 runs, none attributed to page work

check: 0 frames over 100 ms in 95 % of captures (CHECK 90 % met); frames over 250 ms remain in 6 captures of 4 of 9 runs (CHECK not met), and the result names why they are outside the upload path: no script and 0 ms blocking in each attributed frame.
next: BatchPage.tsx:178 (outside OWN) subscribes BatchRecords to the whole upload entry for upload.pending, so every progress publish re-renders the tray; a select on pending would cut that, but it made no frame over 15 ms here. A real-runtime drop with per-10 s captures (scripts/rehearsal, another task) is needed to place S3.8 slow frames in time.
